clue.text: Manage somehow to make bullish adversary elated

parts.note: on the stock market the bear, betting on falling prices, is the opponent of the bull
someone elated is up, in high spirits

explanation.surface: Someone contrives to cheer up a stock-market rival who is betting on a fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manage somehow' is the definition: to bear up is to cope with difficulty. On the stock market a bear expects prices to fall, a bull expects them to rise.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear up is to cope bravely under strain, getting by as best one can.

clue.text: He's tested an explosive in the river

indicators.note: the words an explosive go inside the river's name

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, south-west England
a mine is an explosive device

explanation.surface: Someone checks an explosive device found in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Exe is a river in Devon; crosswords often use it for EXE. 'He's tested' is the definition, a person who sits an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sitting an examination is the person being tested.

clue.text: Make new evaluation of research about Roman coins

indicators.note: research goes around the coins, so its letters sit on either side of them

parts.note: res. is a standard abbreviation of research
the as (plural asses) was a bronze coin of ancient Rome

explanation.surface: A historian re-values findings about a hoard of Roman money.
explanation.walkthrough: RES (short for research) is split around ASSES, giving RE + ASSES + S.
explanation.definitionFit: To reassess is to judge something again, forming a fresh appraisal.

clue.text: Vessel taken by Tommy with some uncertainty

parts.note: Tommy Atkins is slang for a British private soldier
er is the hesitant noise someone makes when unsure

explanation.surface: A ship is commandeered by a hesitant British soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: A Tommy is a British private soldier, from the generic name Tommy Atkins.
explanation.definitionFit: A privateer was an armed, privately owned ship licensed to attack enemy shipping.

clue.text: Sombre after tree gets emergency treatment

indicators.note: the sombre word comes after the tree in the answer

parts.note: a fir is a kind of conifer tree
sombre and staid both mean serious and sober

explanation.surface: Someone gloomy needs urgent help after a run-in with a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places STAID (sombre) behind FIR (tree).
explanation.definitionFit: First aid is the immediate care given to an injured person before a doctor arrives.

clue.text: What an angry, itinerant, unwary witch may do?

definitions.text: What an angry, itinerant, unwary witch may do?

parts.words: What an angry, itinerant, unwary witch may do?
parts.note: an angry person loses their temper; a travelling witch rides a broomstick, and a careless one might fall from it by its stick

explanation.surface: A careless travelling witch in a temper might come off her broomstick.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for losing one's temper is read literally: a witch flying about on a broom could part company with its handle.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to lose one's temper suddenly, which an angry person does.

clue.text: Pole worked the soil and calmed down

parts.note: S is short for south, one of the poles
to till is to plough or cultivate land

explanation.surface: A Polish farmer ploughed the field and relaxed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person, but it is the South Pole, giving S.
explanation.definitionFit: Stilled means made quiet and calm, soothed into tranquillity.

clue.text: Hide copper in a decrepit car? Spot on!

indicators.note: to hide the copper is to tuck it away inside the other pieces

parts.note: crate is slang for an old, broken-down vehicle
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Someone stashes stolen copper in an old banger and is told the idea is perfect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide ... in' tucks CU inside CRATE, after A: A + C(CU)RATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot on is an exclamation meaning exactly right, precise.

clue.text: Act by lackey to gain total control

parts.note: to do is to act
a minion is a servile follower or underling

explanation.surface: A servant's bold move to seize power.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominion is sovereignty, complete authority over a realm.

clue.text: Catastrophe follows a strike in London, say

indicators.note: the strike goes within the city

parts.note: London is an example of a city
to lam is to hit hard

explanation.surface: A disastrous strike paralyses London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'London, say' is the city, not the place of the strike: A + LAM goes inside CITY.
explanation.definitionFit: A calamity is a disaster causing great distress.

clue.text: It's produced by committee for TV series

explanation.surface: A TV comedy made by a committee, as so much television is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produced' rearranges ITS into SIT; COM, short for committee, follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitcom, situation comedy, is a type of television show running in episodes.

clue.text: Court official gives timely hint to workforce

parts.note: a tip is a useful piece of advice
staff are the employees of an organisation

explanation.surface: A court officer gives a well-timed word of advice to the employees.
explanation.walkthrough: A tipstaff is an old legal title for a court officer, a bailiff carrying a metal-tipped staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipstaff is a sheriff's officer or bailiff attending a law court.

clue.text: Left in for wearing old British coin

indicators.note: the letter for left goes inside the word for

parts.note: someone wearing clothes is in them

explanation.surface: An old coin, left behind and kept for wear.
explanation.walkthrough: The florin was a British two-shilling coin, worth ten pence after decimalisation.
explanation.definitionFit: The florin was a two-shilling piece in pre-decimal British currency.

clue.text: Encased in warmth in the hut

parts.note: a shed is a simple hut
heat is warmth

explanation.surface: Someone wraps up warm in a garden hut.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheathed means covered by a protective case, like a sword in its scabbard.

clue.text: A medic ate badly and wasted away

indicators.note: something done badly is messed up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A doctor ate poorly and grew thin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges A MEDIC ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Emaciated means abnormally thin from illness or lack of food.

clue.text: Second setback for her

indicators.note: the second and set are read backwards together

parts.note: taken as the word as written

explanation.surface: A second blow for a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: TESS is the heroine of Hardy's 'Tess of the d'Urbervilles', so 'her' stands for a girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Tess is a female name, standing for any woman referred to as she.

clue.text: Plant keeps French husband in work

indicators.note: the work holds the husband inside it

parts.note: a task is a piece of work
mari is French for husband

explanation.surface: A gardener's plant keeps a Frenchman's husband busy.
explanation.walkthrough: MARI, French for husband, sits inside TASK.
explanation.definitionFit: The tamarisk is a feathery shrub of coastal and dry regions.

clue.text: Thrash youngster first for being evasive

parts.note: to slipper someone is to beat them with a slipper
y is an abbreviation for young

explanation.surface: Give the child a beating first for dodging the question.
explanation.walkthrough: To slipper is old British slang for beating a child with a slipper.
explanation.definitionFit: Slippery describes someone shifty and hard to pin down.

clue.text: Writing article about old gambling game takes an age

indicators.note: the article goes around the game

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
E.O., even-odd, was an 18th-century gambling game

explanation.surface: Writing a piece on an old gambling game takes forever.
explanation.walkthrough: E.O. (even-odd) was a roulette-like game of 18th-century England.
explanation.definitionFit: An aeon is an immensely long period of time.

clue.text: A few admitted to balls make overtures

indicators.note: the few is let into the balls

parts.note: balls are formal dances
V is five in Roman numerals, a few

explanation.surface: A few guests let into the dances make romantic approaches.
explanation.definitionFit: Advances are approaches made to someone, especially romantic overtures.

clue.text: Tour isle in order to see newer rock formations

indicators.note: to put letters in order is to rearrange them

explanation.surface: A geologist tours an island to look at young rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in order' rearranges TOUR ISLE. In geology an outlier is a patch of younger rock surrounded by older rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Geologists use the term for areas of younger strata isolated within older surrounding rock.

clue.text: Unpaid worker given unlimited scope

parts.note: something unpaid for is free
a hand is a manual worker

explanation.surface: An unpaid labourer is given total freedom.
explanation.definitionFit: A free hand is complete freedom to act as one chooses.

clue.text: A sweet, affectionate and tireless worker

parts.note: fond means loving
the ant is proverbially industrious

explanation.surface: A sweet, loving and hardworking person.
explanation.definitionFit: Fondant is a soft sugary confection used in sweets and icing.

clue.text: Attach a couple of pages to epilogue

parts.note: pp. is the abbreviation for pages, p doubled
an epilogue is the end of a work

explanation.surface: Add two pages to the closing section of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: To append is to add something on at the end.

clue.text: Congenial corps in pleasant accommodation

indicators.note: the corps is put inside the pleasant word

parts.note: amiable means friendly and pleasant
C is the abbreviation for corps

explanation.surface: An army unit enjoys comfortable quarters.
explanation.definitionFit: Amicable means friendly and agreeable, without discord.

clue.text: The yeti, for instance

parts.note: the yeti is a manlike creature of Himalayan snow and ice

explanation.surface: The yeti is offered as an example of a creature.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a phrase: a man of the ice, as the abominable snowman is.
explanation.definitionFit: The yeti is a legendary humanlike beast living among ice and snow.

clue.text: After retiring, Edward longed to be uninvolved

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Ted is a short form of Edward
ached means yearned

explanation.surface: Once retired, Edward wanted to stay out of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After retiring' turns TED (Edward) round to DET.
explanation.definitionFit: Detached means aloof, standing apart from events.

clue.text: Two piano features on which all else depends

parts.note: a piano has keys and a tone
tone is the quality of sound a piano produces

explanation.surface: Two parts of a piano, essential to everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A keystone is the central stone of an arch, the principle supporting the rest.

clue.text: Stop daughter going to building sites

indicators.note: building means constructing, so the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A daughter is told not to go near building sites.
explanation.walkthrough: 'building' rearranges SITES into ESIST.
explanation.definitionFit: To desist is to cease doing something.
